finding: `onChange={v => patch({ tool: v, arguments: {} })}` wipes ALL arguments on EVERY Combobox change event, with no `v === step.tool` guard. Base UI's single-select path calls `setSelectedValue(itemValue)` unconditionally on item press (node_modules/@base-ui/react/combobox/root/AriaCombobox.js:563 — no equality check), and the kit's `useControllableState.set` also always fires `onChange` (sdk/packages/kit/src/kit/use-controllable-state.ts:24-26). So re-picking the tool that is ALREADY selected (a natural thing to do when re-opening the picker to check the description, then clicking the highlighted row / pressing Enter) destroys every argument the author entered — both the generated fields and the free rows — with no confirmation and no undo. The kit Combobox is also rendered with `showClear`, so the inline X is a second one-click path to the same silent wipe.

When the picker is active, a saved `step.tool` that is NOT in the fetched tool list renders as EMPTY. The kit Combobox resolves `selected = current ? byValue.get(current) ?? null : null` (sdk/packages/kit/src/kit/combobox.tsx:73) and passes that to Base UI, so an unknown value shows the `placeholder` ("Search this server's tools…"). Failure mode: a workflow saved against tool `search`, which the server later renamed to `web_search`, opens with an apparently BLANK required Tool field while `step.tool` is still `'search'`; `configErrors.tool` (stepForms.ts:209) only checks non-empty so no inline error fires and Save is not blocked. The author cannot see what is stored, and the only way to make the field non-blank is to pick a tool — which (see the finding above) also wipes the arguments.

Non-string enums are handled as strings in both directions. `toolSchemaForm.ts:146` builds options with `value: String(v)`, and this Select commits that string verbatim (`onChange={v => onChange(v)}`, line 152) — so a property declared `{"type":"integer","enum":[1,2,3]}` (the enum branch at toolSchemaForm.ts:157 runs BEFORE the type switch, so it always becomes a select) is saved as the STRING "2" and the tool receives a type it declared it does not accept. The reverse is also broken: the `value` prop is `typeof value === 'string' && value ? value : undefined`, so a workflow loaded with `{"page": 2}` renders the Select as UNSELECTED ("Choose a value") while the argument is in fact set. The same stringification applies to `multiselect` (line 162, `value.map(String)`).

`checked={value === true}` renders a boolean field OFF whenever the key is absent — including when the schema declares `"default": true`. The description below it simultaneously reads "Defaults to true." (line 73), so the author sees a switch in the OFF position next to text saying the default is on, and reasonably concludes the tool will be called with `false`. The control cannot express the three real states (absent/true/false), and there is no way to explicitly send `false` distinct from "leave unset" other than toggling on then off (which does write `false`, since `commitField`'s delete test at ToolStepForm.tsx:213 is strict `=== ''`).

The name→id resolution passes `(servers ?? []).map(...)` UNFILTERED, while the sibling Server picker filters to `s.enabled` (capabilities.tsx:17). A step whose `server` names a DISABLED accessible server therefore renders a Server `Select` showing the placeholder (its option was filtered out, and the kit Select drops an unknown value) while the Tool field below it is a fully populated picker of that same disabled server's tools. The two adjacent controls contradict each other about whether the server exists.

REJECTED (verified, not a defect): I suspected `severityOf` (validationCopy.ts:196-198) would mis-bucket entries from the `warnings` array, because `ValidationError.severity` is OPTIONAL in the generated TS type (api-client/types.ts:7443) and the helper defaults an absent value to 'error' — which would paint a warning with the red XCircle and inflate the red per-step badge in StepList. Checked the wire: `validate.rs:429` declares `severity` as a non-Option field with only `#[serde(default)]` (deserialize-side) and no `skip_serializing_if`, and handlers/dev.rs:951-953 splits the vector BY that field. So every entry landing in `warnings` always carries `severity: "warning"` on the wire. Not reachable.

Template mode is derived from the CURRENT value (`isTemplateValue`), and the plain `Input` used in that mode commits the raw string on every keystroke (line 116). So any PARTIAL edit of a reference flips the field out of template mode mid-typing and silently corrupts the argument. Concrete: a `number`/`integer`/`select`/`switch`/`multiselect` field holding `{{ inputs.limit }}`; the author backspaces the trailing `}}` (or selects-all and types `5`). The value is now the plain string `"{{ inputs.limit "` (or `"5"`), `isTemplateValue` is false, and the control swaps to `InputNumber`/`Select`, whose value guards (`typeof value === 'number'`, line 136; `typeof value === 'string' && value`, line 150) do not match — so the field renders EMPTY. The corrupt string is still in `step.arguments`, invisible and un-editable from the form, and the 'Use a value instead' undo button (line 83) has also disappeared because it only renders while `templated`. The workflow saves with a broken argument the author was shown as blank.

`onChange={v => onChange(v ?? '')}` turns the kit InputNumber's 'still typing' signal into a DELETE. InputNumber emits `undefined` for an intermediate string (`isIntermediate`, sdk/packages/kit/src/kit/input-number.tsx:24/48) — which includes a lone `-` and `1e`. That reaches `commitField` (ToolStepForm.tsx:213), which deletes the key, so the `value` prop becomes `null`, and InputNumber's own sync effect then fires `if (value == null) setBuf('')` (input-number.tsx:33-36) and erases the buffer. Failure mode: in any generated number field the author cannot type a negative value — the `-` vanishes as soon as it is typed. The sibling builder forms avoid this by never letting the value go null (`onChange={v => patch({ max_steps: v ?? 1 })}`, AgentStepForm.tsx:163).

The `json`/`textarea` control runs `coerceToDeclared` on EVERY keystroke, so as soon as the text becomes parseable JSON the stored value becomes an object and `value={valueToText(value)}` re-renders it as `JSON.stringify(...)` — a different string from what the author typed. Typing `{ "a": 1 }` rewrites the textarea to `{"a":1}` the instant the closing brace lands, collapsing the whitespace and moving the caret to the end (React only preserves selection when the controlled value is unchanged). Continuing to type then appends in the wrong place. Coercion belongs on blur, not on change.

Typing a DECLARED property name into a free 'Additional arguments' row makes the row disappear under the author's cursor. `commitRows` (line 203) merges rows last, so the moment the key matches a schema property the value lands in `known`; `splitArguments` then puts it outside `extra`, the resync effect sees `argsSnapshot(extra)` differ from `lastPushed`, and `setRows(argsToRows(extra))` drops the row. The value is not lost (it reappears in the generated field above), but the input the author is typing into is destroyed mid-keystroke with no explanation.

REJECTED (verified sound): I traced the buffer-vs-prop protocol for clobbering. `lastPushed` is written from `rowsToArgs(next)` in `commitRows` while `patch` sends `{...known, ...rowObj}`; the resync effect compares against `argsSnapshot(extra)`, and `extra` is rebuilt in the same key order the merge produced, so `JSON.stringify` equality holds and a self-commit never re-seeds the rows. `commitField` (which does NOT touch `lastPushed`) leaves `extra` byte-identical, so it also does not trip the effect. The generated half and the free half genuinely cannot clobber each other, including across the `useGenerated` false→true transition when the catalog resolves. No finding.

REJECTED (verified clean). `defineLocalStore`'s proxy calls `useStore(...)` on every non-function property read (store-kit.ts:589-593), so a reactive read IS a hook here. I checked every read in the five files: StepList reads `store.def`/`store.selectedStepId`/`store.validation` unconditionally at the top and hoists `findingsByStep` above the `.map()`; BuilderValidationPanel reads `store.validation`/`store.validating`/`store.def` at the top and calls `attributeFindings` before any map; ToolStepForm reads only `catalog.byServerId` (line 122) plus `McpServer.servers`, both unconditional; ToolArgumentsForm/GeneratedField only FORWARD `store` (no property read) and RefInsertMenu's `store.def` read is at the top of its own component, so per-field menus are separate hook scopes. Action reads (`store.selectStep`, `store.updateStep`, `catalog.load`) return function-valued props and take the hook-free branch. Hook counts are stable in all files.

A server that is REACHED but serves ZERO tools degrades SILENTLY — the one case the module's own INV-6 comment (line 111) says must never happen. `entry = {tools: [], loading:false, failure:null}`, so `blockingFailure` is null (no Alert renders) and `usePicker` is false only because `toolOptions.length > 0` fails. The author gets the plain hand-entry `Input` with the generic placeholder 'e.g. search' and the generic description 'The exact name of the tool to call on that server.' — pixel-identical to the pre-picker experience and indistinguishable from 'the picker just hasn't been built for this'. Nothing tells them the server answered and offers nothing (an MCP server whose tool set is permission-filtered to empty, or a misconfigured server, is the realistic case). The store even models the distinction correctly; the component collapses it.

A FAILED validation call is invisible in this panel. `runValidate` (WorkflowBuilder.store.ts:99-107) writes the reason to `store.error` and deliberately keeps the prior `validation` — but `store.error` is not rendered by this panel, nor anywhere else in the builder (WorkflowBuilderPage.tsx renders only `loadError`, `deletedExternally` and save errors). Two wrong states result: (a) if the FIRST validate fails, `validation` is null and this panel asserts 'Add steps to validate the workflow.' while the workflow has steps; (b) if a later validate fails, the panel keeps rendering the stale result — including the green 'No blocking errors.' at line 99 — with no staleness marker, while `saveDisabled` (WorkflowBuilderPage.tsx:68) is computed from that same stale `validation`. In both cases the author is told the workflow validated when it did not.

`LabeledControl` accepts an `error` prop (builderFields.tsx:26) and GeneratedField never passes one, so `required` on a generated field is purely decorative: a missing required argument shows only the red `*`. The backend `POST /validate-def` cannot check arguments against a tool's schema (it never fetches the tool), so nothing else catches it either — the omission surfaces only when the workflow RUNS. The client already knows `field.required` and the current value; the check is one line.

REJECTED (defensively sound). I checked whether a malformed `input_schema` could render an empty or throwing generated section: `describeToolSchema` narrows every access with `isRecord`, returns null for a missing/non-object schema or zero properties (toolSchemaForm.ts:206-212), keeps an unresolvable `$ref` property as a JSON field rather than dropping it (line 233-234), and cuts `$ref` cycles with an explicit stack. So `spec` is either null (caller renders the free-row fallback with the 'Arguments' label) or has at least one field. `ToolArgumentsForm` can never render an empty container.

`data-testid={`wf-builder-finding-goto-${finding.stepId}`}` is not unique: a step with two findings (very common — e.g. a tool step missing both server and tool emits WORKFLOW_TOOL_NO_SERVER and WORKFLOW_TOOL_NO_TOOL, both located at the step id) renders two buttons with the identical testid. Any Playwright `getByTestId(...)` on it fails with a strict-mode violation, so the very affordance this diff adds is not reliably assertable. Index the testid (or key it on the finding code).

The problem/caution badge carries its full phrasing only in a native `title` on a non-focusable `<span>` plus an `sr-only` span. A sighted keyboard user therefore never gets the expansion (`title` shows on hover only, and the span is not tabbable), so for them the badge is a bare glyph and a digit with no stated unit. Screen-reader users are covered by the sr-only text; pointer users by the title; keyboard-only sighted users by neither.

REJECTED (verified named + operable). The new `compact` icon-only trigger passes both `aria-label="Insert reference"` and `tooltip`, and the kit Button's type union FORCES a name on `size="icon"` (button.tsx:59-60) with `aria-label` winning over the tooltip string (button.tsx:97) — so the trigger has an accessible name and is a real `<button>` inside a `Dropdown`. Same for the `Undo2` clear-ref button (ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:89). The empty-refs case still renders a disabled 'No references available yet' item rather than an empty menu (line 38-43). No finding.

REJECTED (pre-existing, not introduced by this diff). The row `<li>` is a clickable non-button with `onClick` and no `role`/`tabIndex`/keyboard handler, which is a genuine a11y gap — but that markup is unchanged from origin/feat/agent-core; the diff only adds the validation badges inside it. Out of scope as a finding against this branch.

REJECTED (conformant). Checked every class added by the diff across all five files: colors are semantic tokens only (`text-destructive`, `text-warning`, `text-muted-foreground`, `bg-muted`, `border-primary`, `bg-accent`) — no raw hue, no arbitrary color value, no inline style color. Direction props are logical throughout (`text-start`, `ps-0`, `justify-start`, `items-start`); no `pl/pr`, `ml/mr`, `text-left/right` appears in the diff. Spacing stays on the 4px scale plus the kit's sanctioned 2px half-steps (`mt-0.5`, `py-1`). `SectionHeader` is already used for the Steps title+actions row (StepList.tsx:53), form fields go through `LabeledControl` rather than raw flex-gap, and every control is a kit component — no raw `<button>`/`<input>`.

The label-row action group has no `shrink-0`, and `LabeledControl`'s row is `flex items-center justify-between gap-2` with a `<label>` that has neither `min-w-0` nor truncation (builderFields.tsx:57-62). The labels here come from the tool's schema `title` (toolSchemaForm.ts:238) and can be long. At ~358px (the config column at a 390px viewport) a long single-token label pushes against the two icon buttons, which — having only `w-8`-style width and default `flex-shrink: 1` — compress rather than hold their size. The `compact` variant addresses the width of the trigger but not its shrink behaviour; `shrink-0` on the wrapper is the fix.

REJECTED (holds up). Traced the new kind-Tag + badge row at the narrowest real case. The page stacks below `md` (WorkflowBuilderPage.tsx:184-187) so at 390px the list is full-width, and at `md` the column is `w-80` (320px) minus the grip and three icon buttons. The wrapper carries `min-w-0`, the Tag carries `min-w-0 truncate`, and both badges carry `shrink-0 whitespace-nowrap` — so the kind label truncates and the counts stay intact rather than wrapping to a second line. No overflow.

REJECTED as a coupling violation: `import { McpServer } from '@/modules/mcp/stores/mcpServer'` matches the established house pattern here — the sibling `capabilities.tsx:3` does exactly this and its header calls `McpServer` 'the sanctioned cross-module accessor', and `AgentStepForm.tsx:8` imports it too. Not a new cross-module reach. (The real problem is that ToolStepForm re-derives the server list itself instead of reusing the module's own helper, which is what causes the enabled-filter divergence logged separately under correctness-logic.)

REJECTED. `ToolArgumentsForm` takes the whole `WorkflowBuilderStore` purely to forward it to `RefInsertMenu`, which is a wider dependency than the component needs — but it is the same threading pattern `PromptField` already uses (builderFields.tsx:76-77), and `RefInsertMenu`'s own contract requires the store. Not worth changing, and not a coupling violation.

The tool catalog is refetched over the network on EVERY step selection. `ToolCatalogStoreDef.use()` is a `defineLocalStore`, whose `use()` builds a fresh store per component INSTANCE (store-kit.ts:634-648: `useRef` seeded once per mount), and `StepConfigPanel` remounts the form on every switch via `<StepForm key={step.id}>` (StepConfigPanel.tsx:88). So `byServerId` starts empty on each mount, the store's own cache short-circuit (`existing && !existing.loading && existing.failure == null`, ToolCatalog.store.ts:59) can never hit, and clicking between two tool steps on the same server issues a `GET /api/mcp/servers/{id}/tools` each time — a call that for a stdio server can mean spawning/handshaking the server process. It is also visible: during each refetch `usePicker` is false, so the Tool field renders as a DISABLED plain Input and then swaps back to a Combobox, and the 'Additional arguments' section briefly shows every declared argument as a free key/value row before the effect re-partitions them.

REJECTED (not a real cost). `attributeFindings` runs unmemoized twice in this panel and twice more in StepList on every render, and `commitRows`/`commitField` write the store on every keystroke. But `attributeFindings` is O(findings × steps) over a list the backend caps at 50 steps and a handful of findings, and the per-keystroke store write is the pre-existing builder pattern used by every other step form. No re-render storm and no expensive derive.

The 'Tool list unavailable' Alert is terminal — it offers no retry, so an `unreachable` failure (a server that was briefly down) can only be cleared by navigating away and back. The store ships `invalidate(serverId)` specifically for this, documented as 'used by "try again"' (ToolCatalog.store.ts:117-118), and it has no caller anywhere in the app; `markUnknown` and the `unknownNames` state it writes (ToolCatalog.store.ts:47/111) likewise have no production reader — grepped both UI workspaces. Either wire a retry action into this Alert or drop the unreachable store surface.

`spec.overflowNames` is only ever length-checked; the names themselves are never rendered. The note says 'Showing N of M arguments this tool accepts — the rest can be set below', but 'below' is a free key/value editor and `splitArguments` only creates a row for an overflow property that ALREADY has a saved value — so for a tool declaring >24 properties the author is told extra arguments exist and given no way to learn a single one of their names. The data to fix it is already computed and carried into the component.

REJECTED. The new `compact` prop is reached on a production path — `ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:104` passes it for every generated field — and the labelled default branch is still used by `PromptField` (builderFields.tsx:111-116). Both branches live. Likewise `AttributedFinding.stepIndex`/`stepLabel` are consumed by `findingStepTitle`, and `WORKFLOW_LEVEL` is used inside `indexFindingsByStep`. No dead additions in these files.
